name: Rotom
title: How I build
flavour: Bzzt! Spec in, reviewed PR out.
what: An agent loop for BubblyChef. One GitHub issue labelled ready-for-agent goes in. A planned, tested, browser-verified and twice-reviewed PR comes out, opened by a separate bot account.
how: Control flow lives in code, judgement lives in agents. A script decides every stop, retry and merge permission from facts the agents report. Stages: plan, implement, verify in a real browser, review, ship.
impact: It's now a template: the same process runs this portfolio's agent loop, from brief to review to PR.

built.title: Spec
built.text: Write the spec and split it into ready-for-agent GitHub issues.

built.title: Agent
built.text: Plan, implement, and verify in a real browser. A fresh-context reviewer then checks the diff.

built.title: Review
built.text: The bot opens the PR. GitHub's own review and CI gates check it, and Ayush reviews anything irreversible.

learned.title: Pilot failures
learned.text: Most of the 21 runs are one pilot failure turned into a rule no agent can skip.

learned.title: Fit
learned.text: It earns its keep on from-scratch issues with a clear spec, and is overkill for rebases and fix-ups.

name: BubblyChef
title: BubblyChef
flavour: Bzzt! Scans receipts, reads the pantry
and cooks from what is really there.

ribbon.text: Built with the agent loop · 21 runs

what: An AI-first kitchen app with receipt scanning, pantry-aware recipe generation, grocery list automation and a natural-language chat assistant.
how: Recipes are grounded in the real pantry inventory, and recipes import from social media and websites. A Next.js front end talks to a LangGraph AI service.
impact: Snap a receipt and the pantry fills itself; dinner ideas start from what's about to expire. Ayush reaches for it when cooking a fuller meal; a mobile app is next, to make it an everyday tool.

built.title: Solo
built.text: One developer, with the agent loop's bot account writing about half the commits.

built.title: Agent loop
built.text: Issues labelled ready-for-agent became reviewed PRs from a bot account, over 21 runs of the loop.

built.title: Live
built.text: Public on GitHub and live on Vercel.

learned.title: Issue quality
learned.text: A loop is only as good as its issue, and the human ideas and understanding behind it. In one batch of about 10 PRs, 7 issues had a wrong or incomplete premise.

learned.title: Cohesion
learned.text: How to turn a pile of features into one cohesive app experience.

name: TradeDesk
title: TradeDesk
flavour: Bzzt! A trade journal with replay.
Planned with Fable, built by agents.
what: A local-only trade journal with a bar-replay backtester, sharing one database and one analytics engine. Agents built the first version; Ayush hasn't put it to real use yet.
how: The journal groups filled orders into round-trip trades, with a P&L calendar and win rate. Replay steps 1-minute candles bar by bar with no lookahead, and simulated trades flow into the same journal.
impact: Ayush will journal every real trade and practise setups in replay; both land in one set of stats, so he can see what works before putting money on it.

built.title: Idea
built.text: It started as one big, high-level idea. Fable, then in early access, turned it into a detailed, hands-off spec.

built.title: Autonomous build
built.text: Ayush orchestrated the build with Opus agents, an early version of his agent loop, and it ran almost entirely hands-off.

built.title: Review
built.text: Understanding of the code slipped, so Ayush paused it to review before building more.

learned.title: Broker data
learned.text: Financial data is messy: fills have to be grouped into round-trip trades before any stat means anything.

learned.title: Keep up
learned.text: Autonomous building is fast, but understanding slips. Review before you build more.

name: Stave
title: Stave
flavour: Bzzt! Big pages, one tap to turn,
and a left hand it can rewrite.
what: A personal sheet-music reader and arranger for the tablet. Scores are big and reflowed, and pages turn by tap, keys or a Bluetooth pedal.
how: Arrange tools rewrite the left hand, roll chords, fix wide stretches, transpose and label chords. An Ask agent plans the edits, and you can pick a range of measures.
impact: Ayush practises from it on his tablet. He built it to fix daily practice pain: MuseScore is clunky on a tablet, fingerings can't be edited, and marking up PDFs by hand is slow.

built.title: v0
built.text: A tablet score viewer and the first arrange tools, committed on Sep 30, 2026.

built.title: Background build
built.text: On Oct 1, an agent built the Ask arrange agent, tap-to-select measures, and Find a score (links only).

built.title: Local
built.text: It runs on Ayush's PC and is not deployed publicly.

learned.title: One registry
learned.text: The arrange buttons and the Ask agent use the same tool schemas.

learned.title: Validate
learned.text: Edits that break measure lengths, overlap, or leave the keyboard are rejected.
